scope: Authentication backlog pressure, durable event catch-up, multi-session tools and real TCP backpressure

implementation.queue: Per-connection per-session afterSeq/throughSeq metadata; event payloads remain persisted
implementation.databaseRead: Exact next sequence through the session/seq covering index; MIN(rowid) merges candidates before loading one payload
databasePlan: SEARCH events USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid=?)
SEARCH candidate USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_events_2 (session_id=? AND seq=?)
implementation.memory: Connection cursor metadata grows with pending sessions; process one event at a time, rather than retaining all payloads
implementation.send: Wait for the ws.send callback before fetching another event; yield after every 32 events

coverage: 1200 synthetic persisted events across four sessions survive successful real account refresh without disconnect
12 synthetic persisted events totaling 4722062 bytes survive successful real account refresh without disconnect
Global append order, per-session sequences, exactly-once live delivery and paginated durable history
Original real write-tool scenario and two concurrent write-tool sessions do not replay side effects
Real Core 401 and changed account identity close only the affected connection and send no held events
Account RPC and Blob isolation, restart persistence and credential boundaries
Real paused TCP receiver resumes to receive all 256 frames while another connection progresses
Real continuously paused TCP receiver times out with 1013 while another connection remains live

limitations: Synthetic pressure events and recorded models do not measure real provider quality or production-scale capacity.
Production browser transport ran in Node/Vite; no visible Electron UI was exercised.
No long-running soak, operating-system memory exhaustion or full repository suite was run.
Ordinary RPC responses retain their preexisting network buffer protection; unrelated real sequence gaps still reconnect the shared WebSocket.
The previously baseline-confirmed ownership rename failure remains a separate issue.
Running user services have not been replaced or restarted.
